title: Lizard Boy once again cementing that I really need to go to Edinburgh...
transcript: I absolutely love musical theatre. I think it is one of the hardest things to make. But every year I feel like I can find at least one really good, obscure off Broadway musical that just makes me fall in love with the craft again. I saw a couple of these last year, particularly Islander, which I absolutely adored. And already we have a strong contender for this year's musical, Lizard Boy. The elevator pitch for Lizard Boy is that it's an unapologetically queer superhero story. It has only 3 performers. They all play the instruments as well as performing, and it's a very simple story of boy meets Lizard Boy, complicated by potentially having to save the world. The show is charming and fun to watch, and it's definitely not a perfect show. It's a little scrappy and rough around the edges, but it almost makes it that much more endearing. Definitely recommend this show if you are thinking of producing your own shows or directing your own shows, especially with a low budget, because just what this show does with the space and with the materials that it's given is so inventive. The movement of the performers, the way that they utilize the props around them, the way that they utilize their instruments that they are playing for the show is just so inventive, and it's one of those moments that makes you just re fall in love with theater as a medium. This is the first show By writer Justin Horatus, who wrote this as well as stars in it, and I'm really excited for his future work. I would say that if you like the stylings of Ryan Scott Oliver or Rick Riordan, you're going to enjoy this musical, especially if you like shows like The Lightning Thief and Jasper and Deadland. In fact, Brandon Ivy, who directed the show, also directed the world premiere of Jasper and Deadland. And if you can't make it to New York, you can still listen to it. They do have a cast recording available. This is pretty old. I feel like the sound has matured a lot from this, but a lot of the songs are the same boys. Currently playing on Theatre Row until July first, so you have just a couple weeks to catch this one, but I definitely think it's worth checking out, especially if you love inventive theater.
